Benjamin Flores

Democratic candidate for Commissioner of the General Land Office, Texas · Challenger

Bay City City Council member; cybersecurity and risk management professional

Benjamin Flores is a Democrat, a Bay City City Council member and a cybersecurity and risk management professional who came to the U.S. from Mexico City in 1996. He first announced a run for governor in April 2025, then left that race to run for Texas Land Commissioner. He beat Jose Loya in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and faces incumbent Dawn Buckingham (R) and Neill Snider (L) on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

Where Flores stands

Disaster recovery
Says Hurricane Harvey families waited eight years for recovery money. Pledges that disaster recovery will take months, not years, if he is elected.
Veterans programs
Proposes cutting Veterans Land Board loan wait times from six months to six weeks and making the board's programs easier to access.
Public school funding / Permanent School Fund
Supports raising General Land Office revenue to fund public schools and lower property taxes.
Energy leasing / revenue diversification
Supports adding more renewable energy projects on state lands to bring in more revenue, according to the Austin American-Statesman editorial board.
Coastal protection
Supports protecting coastal communities from storms.
Agency management and transparency
Says his priority is transparent management of Texas lands. Argues the GLO needs competent management instead of culture-war fights.

Background

  • Member, Bay City City Council
  • Board member, Bay City Development Corporation
  • Bay City representative, Houston-Galveston Area Council
  • About 30-year career in cybersecurity and risk management
  • Started a family business raising pigs
  • Studied geography at Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM)
  • Announced a run for Texas governor (April 2025); left that race to run for Land Commissioner
  • Won the Democratic primary for Texas Land Commissioner (March 3, 2026)
  • Announced a leukemia diagnosis (June 2026) and later said he was in remission; stayed in the race
